subject: ENGLISH 2
description: ICSE 10th English Literature: Shakespeare's Julius Caesar (Acts 3, 4 and 5)

questions.question: Which conspirator was the first to strike and stab Julius Caesar in the Senate?
questions.explanation: Casca struck first, shouting: 'Speak, hands, for me!' in Act 3, Scene 1.

questions.question: What famous opening phrase does Mark Antony use in his funeral oration to address the Roman crowd?
options: Romans, countrymen, and lovers! hear me for my cause
Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears
Citizens of Rome, awake your senses
Hear me, noble Romans, for Caesar's sake
questions.explanation: Antony's speech begins: 'Friends, Romans, countrymen, lend me your ears; I come to bury Caesar, not to praise him.'

questions.question: Whose cut does Antony describe as 'the most unkindest cut of all' on Caesar's mantle?
questions.explanation: Antony highlights Brutus' cut as the most unkindest cut because Caesar deeply loved Brutus as an angel.

questions.question: What ghost appears to Brutus in his tent near Sardis before the Battle of Philippi?
questions.explanation: The Ghost of Caesar appears, declaring itself Brutus' evil spirit and promising to see him at Philippi.

questions.question: Why did Cassius order his servant Pindarus to slay him at the Battle of Philippi?
options: He was surrounded by Antony's troops
He mistakenly believed his dear friend Titinius had been captured
He suffered a mortal sword wound
questions.explanation: Cassius mistakenly believed Titinius was taken by enemy troops, leading him to end his own life prematurely.

questions.question: At the close of the play, who praises Brutus as 'the noblest Roman of them all'?
questions.explanation: Antony honors Brutus because alone among the conspirators, he acted from an honest, general good to all Romans.
